notes:
All 65 stations are matched. 60 have a Findlay row. The other 5 are null: two observer stations that are not lights (Fair Isle, Hynish Signal Tower) and three that are not in the 1879 edition (North Carr L.V., Fidra, Ailsa Craig). Each of these 3 appears in the reports only from 1885. Hoy Low and Hoy High share row 238. No station needed extra_rows: every multi-light station is printed in a single row (Pentland Skerries 234, Isle of May 204, Girdleness 216, Monach Isles 254, Stornoway 253, Pladda 274, Hoy 238). I checked each match by position and coast order as well as by name.

Things to check:
(1) Gaps and unclear readings in the transcription: Rhuvaal (266) has no year. Lamlash/Holy Isle (275) reads '[?]877' and Little Ross (291) reads '184[?]'. Look at the scans if you need those years.
(2) Two Montrose rows: 213 MONTROSE NESS is the lighthouse (Scurdie Ness); 214 is the harbour lights. There are also two Loch Ryan rows: 286 is the lighthouse; 287 Stranraer is the piers.
(3) The Isle Ornsay row is printed 'Oronsay Island'. It is in Sleat Sound, not at Oronsay off Colonsay.
(4) Findlay's coast headings differ from the report regions. Start Point, North Ronaldsay and the Shetland lights fall under 'North & West Coasts' on p.49, while Auskerry, Hoy and Cantick are under 'East Coast'. Use the positions for anything that depends on coast.
(5) Findlay prints Glass Island after Monach Isles, so its order there differs from the reports'. The reports' own neighbour lists also disagree around Ushenish and Monach. This did not affect any match.
(6) The 1879 list has a Tay River light-vessel (208), but it is marked 'Intended' and has nothing to do with North Carr.
(7) Muckle Flugga is once printed 'North Uist' in the reports, a slip for North Unst. Its region is marked 'unknown' in the station table.
